record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: The number of k-power-free binary words of length n grows polynomially with n for k ≤ 7/3, but exponentially for k > 7/3 [24]. Examine analogous results for alphabets of arbitrary size.

evidence.quote: The number of k-power-free binary words of length n grows polynomially with n for k ≤ 7/3, but exponentially for k > 7/3 [24]. Examine analogous results for alphabets of arbitrary size.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Σ_q denote a finite alphabet of size q ≥ 2, and let Σ_q^* be the set of all finite words over Σ_q. For a real number k > 1, a word w = w_1 w_2 ... w_n ∈ Σ_q^* is said to contain a k-power if there exist indices i and a positive integer p with i + ⌈kp⌉ - 1 ≤ n such that w_{j+p} = w_j for all 0 ≤ j ≤ ⌈kp⌉ - 1 - p; equivalently, w contains a factor of the form x^k = x x x ... where x has length p and the factor has length ⌈kp⌉. A word is k-power-free if it contains no k-power, and is k^+-power-free if it contains no k'-power for any k' > k. Let L_q(k) ⊆ Σ_q^* denote the language of k-power-free words over Σ_q, and let f_{q,k}(n) = |L_q(k) ∩ Σ_q^n| be the number of such words of length n.

It is known that for q = 2, the function f_{2,k}(n) grows polynomially in n when k ≤ 7/3, but grows exponentially in n when k > 7/3. 

Determine, for every alphabet size q ≥ 3, the threshold value k_q ∈ ℝ (and the behaviour at the threshold, distinguishing k-power-free from k^+-power-free) such that f_{q,k}(n) grows polynomially in n for k ≤ k_q and exponentially in n for k > k_q. In particular, establish whether the analogue of the binary dichotomy holds for arbitrary q, identify the critical exponent k_q, and describe the asymptotic behaviour of the exponential growth rate

   α(q, k) = lim_{n → ∞} f_{q,k}(n)^{1/n}

as q → ∞ for fixed k > 1, and as k decreases to k_q for fixed q.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Shur and collaborators studied growth rates of power-free languages over arbitrary alphabets, identifying the critical exponent and proving asymptotic formulas for α(q,k) when k ≥ 2. A 2025 result (MFCS 2025) proves Shur's conjecture on the growth of (n/(n-1))-free and (n/(n-1))^+-free languages over q-letter alphabets up to a correction of order O(1/q²). Threshold-word growth on n letters is also known to be exponential. However, a complete dichotomy theorem characterizing the polynomial-vs-exponential threshold for every alphabet size, analogous to the 7/3 result for q=2, is not fully resolved in general.

status_evidence.title: A Proof of Shur's Conjecture on the Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Shur's conjecture on growth rates of (n/(n-1))-free and (n/(n-1))^+-free languages over q-letter alphabets settled up to O(1/q^2).
status_evidence.claim: Partial resolution of growth-rate conjectures for power-free languages over arbitrary alphabets.

status_evidence.title: Growth of Power-Free Languages over Large Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies α(k,β), the exponential growth rate of β-power-free languages over k-letter alphabets, with asymptotics for β ≥ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic results for the exponential growth rate over large alphabets are established.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial versus Exponential Growth in Repetition-Free Binary Words
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the 7/3 threshold for polynomial vs exponential growth in the binary case.
status_evidence.claim: The original binary dichotomy result that motivates the problem.

status_evidence.title: The Number of Threshold Words on n Letters Grows Exponentially
status_evidence.snippet: Shows exponential growth of threshold words over n-letter alphabets.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms exponential growth at threshold exponents for general alphabet sizes.
